messages:
maria: Heads up — ran the nightly replay harness on gpu-12.2 image and saw ~15% worse p95 compared to gpu-12.1 image. Synthetic load didn't show this. Looking for ideas where env drift could cause kernel selection / kv/cache behavior differences.

sam: hmm, do we have exact image tags?

maria: redwood/runtime:gpu-ubuntu22.04-cuda12.1-2025-11-08 vs redwood/runtime:gpu-ubuntu22.04-cuda12.2-2026-01-20 (driver 535 vs 540 on the nodes).

kevin: Did you keep the same model binary / quant profile? small version bumps can flip kernel selector heuristics.

maria: yes pinned the model artifact and quant profile. only thing that changed was base image + driver.

ryan: two quick guesses: 1) cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel fallback behavior changed and our kernel selector picks a different kernel for certain sequence lengths. 2) different driver/CUDA might expose different timing for async kernels -> batching heuristics timing window triggers differently.

maria: exactly what I'm thinking. replay shows extra small allocations around kv-prefetch phases and some extra context switch noise in the trace. p95 spikes align with cache warmups.

tanya: can you share the perf traces? nvprof/nsight or logs?

maria: pasted the short trace snippet below:```
# nvprof timeline (simplified)
[00:12.122] conv2d.forward    3.4ms  (cutlass_kernel_x)
[00:12.126] matmul.forward    1.9ms  (cublasLt)
[00:12.129] kv-prefetch       0.7ms  (custom-kv-copy)
[00:12.130] matmul.forward    3.6ms  (cutlass_kernel_y)
# On cuda12.1 image we saw matmul 1.8ms then 1.7ms for the same ops (consistent)
```

sam: That matmul change suggests a different algorithm selection inside cublasLt/cutlass. Are the workspace sizes/algorithm heuristics the same?

kevin: Also check environment vars: `CUTLASS_TUNING=auto` or any `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` changes. Containers sometimes carry different defaults.

maria: I dumped env from both images:```
# cuda12.1 image env subset
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
CUTLASS_TUNING=off
TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
# cuda12.2 image env subset
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=
CUTLASS_TUNING=auto
TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
```

ryan: there you go — CUTLASS_TUNING=auto may pick different kernels at runtime causing slight variance across batched matmuls, which can affect tail latencies when combined with KV prefetch timing.

maria: interesting — but why would synthetic load not show this? synthetic tests use idealized sequence lengths (all short) while replay has a mix and KV cache warmup patterns. The kernel selector may choose different algo based on problem shapes seen in the wild.

kevin: action plan: 1) reproduce locally by forcing CUTLASS_TUNING=off on the cuda12.2 image and re-run replay; 2) capture kernel selection logs (enable CUTLASS debug/verbose if possible) and cublasLt algorithm IDs; 3) run a small replay subset that cross-covers long-short sequence transitions to stress KV warmups.

maria: started job 1918001125 with CUTLASS_TUNING=off on cuda12.2 image, replay subset (prefix lengths varied). I'll post results.

deploy-bot: job 1918001125 queued on iam-runner-07 (nvidia-a100-sxm4) using image redwood/runtime:gpu-ubuntu22.04-cuda12.2-2026-01-20. Estimated duration: 18m.

sam: also add a run where we toggle `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb` to smaller to see allocation fragmentation impact — sometimes allocator can delay kernel dispatch.

maria: good call. queued a follow-up job 1918001150 with CUTLASS_TUNING=auto + TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64.

ryan: if CUTLASS tuning fixes it, we should treat that env var as a platform default and enforce it in our container images for parity. If not, we look at driver differences and cuBLAS patch notes between 535 and 540.

maria: first run (1918001125) finished: p95 down to baseline (within 1%) when CUTLASS_TUNING=off. Logs show algorithm id stable across sequence lengths. Attaching short excerpt:```
# kernel selection excerpt
matmul(shape=64x64) -> cutlass_algo_12 (deterministic)
matmul(shape=64x128) -> cutlass_algo_12
```

kevin: confirms selector divergence is primary suspect. Great find.

maria: follow-up run (1918001150) with smaller split_size still had small variance (~3% p95) — not full regression but worse than when tuning off.

ryan: next steps: 1) standardize CUTLASS_TUNING=off in our gpu image builds to match synthetic harness; 2) update replay harness to include mixed sequence transitions as part of the baseline; 3) add a kernel-selection audit in the perf pipeline that surfaces algorithm id histograms per run.

tanya: will create a quick RFC for image env defaults and add to the release checklist. tagging infra to help with image rebuild. @maria can you paste the minimal repro command you used so infra can replicate?

maria: repro command:```
# run on node with image set and env overrides
docker run --gpus all -e CUTLASS_TUNING=off -e TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 \
  redwood/runtime:gpu-ubuntu22.04-cuda12.2-2026-01-20 \
  /bin/bash -c "./run_replay.sh --subset mixed-transition --duration 5m"
```

maria: I'll open a short PR to set CUTLASS_TUNING=off in the image and add a perf check to the replay job. Also adding a unit in the perf dashboard for algorithm-id distributions.

kevin: Awesome. Also we should add a note in the runbook: when you see p95 regressions on new driver images, first check container env vars that enable autotune heuristics.

maria: +1. filing follow-ups now. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: thread auto-archive scheduled in 30 days.
